proposed_widenings.name: grant_die_token
proposed_widenings.justification: The core mechanic hands a held die to a third-party creature. The token lives on the recipient (not the caster), has a 1-hour expiry, and is activated reactively by the recipient on their own rolls. No v4 atom captures a held, single-use, transferable die resource owned by a creature other than the activating caster.
proposed_widenings.evidence: That creature gains one of your Bardic Inspiration dice. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.

proposed_widenings.name: die_token_activation_subgraph
proposed_widenings.justification: The recipient activates the token reactively: on failing a D20 Test within 1 hour, they roll the die and add it to the d20. This is a two-actor post-roll pattern with cross-actor resource ownership and a per-holder expiry. v4 has post_roll_window and modify_roll_numeric but lacks the holder-side activation chain and the cross-actor ownership model needed to wire them together honestly.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Once within the next hour when the creature fails a D20 Test, the creature can roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning the failure into a success. A Bardic Inspiration die is expended when it's rolled.

proposed_widenings.name: UseCountCap: ability_score_derived
proposed_widenings.justification: Uses equal the bard's Charisma modifier (minimum 1). This is an ability-score-derived count that changes with character build, not a fixed integer or a threshold-tiered schedule keyed to class level. UseCountCap currently only supports fixed and threshold_tiers.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can confer a Bardic Inspiration die a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once)

notes: The two-actor token mechanic is the fundamental blocker: the bard hands a die to another creature which holds it and uses it reactively on failure. This cross-actor resource delegation has no existing subgraph. The die-size scaling (d6→d8→d10→d12 at bard levels 1/5/10/15) is expressible via ThresholdTiers<DiceExprDelta> with dieSize overrides once the token atom exists — that part is not a gap. The cha-mod use count is a secondary surface gap. No dhall/json/trace produced: forced a misleading trace would be worse than no trace.
